cards.a: Inside the Project Presentation itself - a strong presentation includes at least one explicit comparison to your own community - and it can resurface in the Project Q&A if a question asks about your personal connection to the topic.
cards.n: The skill was not dropped, only relocated - keep practicing it.

cards.q: Explain how the 2027 redesign changed the way readers score each free-response task, compared with the old exam.
cards.a: The old holistic rubric (one single 0-5 band judging everything at once) is replaced by an analytic, point-based rubric: each task is scored dimension by dimension - task completion and development, organization, and language control - and the points are added together.
cards.n: An analytic rubric means one weak dimension does not automatically drag every other dimension down with it.

cards.q: State how the Argumentative Essay is scored on the 2027 rubric.
cards.a: On a published point-based analytic rubric worth 10 points, awarded across five separate categories rather than one holistic band. Broadly they cover task completion and argumentation (a defensible thesis, use of all three sources, a counterargument), organization and cohesion, and language control (vocabulary range, grammar accuracy, register).
cards.n: Points are awarded category by category, so a near-perfect thesis cannot rescue an essay that cites one source. Check the current CED for the exact category names.

cards.q: State how the Project Presentation is scored on the 2027 rubric.
cards.a: On a published point-based analytic rubric worth 11 points across five separate categories — the most heavily weighted single task on the exam, at 20% of the score. Broadly they cover task completion and development (answering the guiding question, cultural content, the comparison to your own community), organization and signposting, and language control (vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, register).
cards.n: Nervous pauses cost language control, not task completion — a well-organised answer still earns its points there. Check the current CED for the exact category names.

cards.q: State how the Project Q&A is scored on the 2027 rubric, and how many questions it asks.
cards.a: Four pre-recorded questions, about 40 seconds to answer each, scored on a published point-based analytic rubric worth 9 points across several categories rather than one holistic band. They reward directly addressing the question asked, sustaining and elaborating the exchange, and language control under spontaneous timed conditions.
cards.n: Because it is spontaneous, language control is judged more forgivingly here than on the typed essay. Check the current CED for the exact category names.

cards.q: Define what 'maintains the exchange' means to an AP reader scoring the Project Q&A.
cards.a: Your answer directly and appropriately addresses what the question actually asked, in a way that keeps the exchange moving naturally - as opposed to ignoring the question, changing the subject, or giving an answer generic enough to fit any question.
cards.h: → definition, contrast with what fails it
cards.n: A fluent, grammatically perfect answer to the wrong question still fails to maintain the exchange.

cards.q: Define 'elaboration' the way an AP reader uses the term, and give the minimum shape that counts as elaborated.
cards.a: Going beyond a bare direct answer to add a reason, an example, a detail, or a consequence. The minimum: one full extra clause connected with a word like parce que, ce qui, or par exemple - not the same idea repeated in longer words.
cards.n: Repeating your answer in different words is not elaboration; readers are trained to spot the difference.

cards.q: Contrast a Project Q&A answer that merely answers with one that elaborates, for the question 'Pourquoi ce sujet vous intéresse-t-il ?'
cards.a: Merely answers: 'Ce sujet m'intéresse parce que c'est important.' Elaborates: 'Ce sujet m'intéresse parce que ma grand-mère a vécu cette réalité en Haïti, ce qui a rendu mes recherches personnelles dès le départ.'
cards.n: The elaborated version reuses the question's structure and adds one concrete, personal detail - exactly what raises the score.

cards.q: Donne trois formules de haut niveau pour exprimer une conséquence ou un résultat.
cards.a: Par conséquent, ... / Ainsi, ... / De ce fait, ...
cards.n: Vary these across an essay instead of repeating donc every time - repetition reads as thin vocabulary.

cards.q: Donne trois formules de haut niveau pour introduire une cause ou une explication.
cards.a: Étant donné que... / Dans la mesure où... / Cela s'explique par le fait que...
cards.n: Étant donné que and dans la mesure où both take the indicative, not the subjunctive - a common student error is adding one out of habit.

cards.q: Donne deux structures pour formuler une hypothèse ou une condition dans un essai argumentatif, avec un exemple pour chacune.
cards.a: Si + présent, ... futur : Si cette tendance se poursuit, la situation s'aggravera. / À condition que + subjonctif : ... à condition que les autorités agissent rapidement.
cards.n: Si always takes the indicative, never the subjunctive - mixing them (si ce soit) is one of the most common formal-register errors.

cards.q: Donne trois formules de haut niveau pour souligner l'importance d'un point.
cards.a: Il est primordial de... / Il importe de souligner que... / Ce point mérite une attention particulière.
cards.n: Il est primordial de + infinitif keeps the sentence impersonal and formal - avoid je pense que c'est important.

cards.q: Cite trois mots utiles pour un essai sur le monde du travail.
cards.a: le télétravail (remote work) / la précarité (job insecurity) / le déséquilibre vie professionnelle-vie privée (work-life imbalance).
cards.n: La précarité is the word graders notice, and its adjective is précaire, as in un emploi précaire.

cards.q: Cite trois mots utiles pour un essai sur l'identité et l'immigration.
cards.a: l'intégration (integration) / le multiculturalisme (multiculturalism) / le déracinement (uprooting, loss of one's roots).
cards.n: Le déracinement is the high-value word here; pair it with les racines and se sentir déraciné for range.

cards.q: Cite trois mots utiles pour un essai sur l'éducation.
cards.a: la réussite scolaire (academic success) / le décrochage scolaire (dropping out) / l'inégalité des chances (unequal opportunity).
cards.n: Le décrochage comes from décrocher, to drop out, and the student concerned is un décrocheur or une décrocheuse.

cards.q: Cite trois mots utiles pour un essai sur l'environnement, différents de ceux d'un répertoire de base (gaspillage, écologique).
cards.a: l'empreinte carbone (carbon footprint) / la transition énergétique (energy transition) / la biodiversité (biodiversity).
cards.n: L'empreinte carbone is feminine, and its usual verbs are réduire, compenser and calculer son empreinte.

cards.q: Explain why using the subjunctive correctly after expressions like il faut que and bien que raises your language-control score, beyond simple grammatical accuracy.
cards.a: The subjunctive is a marker of grammatical range and formal register - readers are trained to notice varied structures, not just accuracy. An essay using only the indicative reads as simple even when it is error-free.
cards.n: Bien que forces the subjunctive even though the fact conceded is objectively true - a frequent slip.

cards.q: Decide: should you ever address the audience as tu instead of vous in the Project Presentation or Project Q&A?
cards.a: No. Both are addressed to an unknown evaluator in an academic context - vous is the only appropriate choice unless a prompt explicitly has you quoting yourself speaking to a specific, informal person.
cards.n: Slipping into tu drags the wrong verb endings along with it, so one lapse tends to spread through the whole answer.

cards.q: Donne deux formules pour exprimer une certitude nuancée, ni trop timide ni trop absolue.
cards.a: Il est fort probable que + indicatif... / Tout porte à croire que...
cards.n: Avoid both je suis sûr que (too absolute for an argumentative essay) and peut-être (too weak) - these two sit in between.

cards.q: Donne trois formules pour relier une donnée chiffrée à son explication, sans répéter 'ce qui montre que'.
cards.a: Ce chiffre traduit... / Cela reflète... / Ces données témoignent de...
cards.n: Varying the link-verb (traduit, reflète, témoigne de) instead of always ce qui montre que raises the vocabulary-range signal readers look for.

cards.q: Sujet : « Le télétravail profite-t-il davantage aux employés ou aux entreprises ? » Écris une phrase de thèse qui prend clairement position.
cards.a: Nous soutiendrons que, malgré les avantages qu'il procure aux entreprises, le télétravail profite avant tout aux employés en leur rendant un temps et une autonomie précieux.
cards.n: Notice davantage from the prompt reappears as avant tout, showing you engaged with the exact question asked.

cards.q: Sujet : « Les jeunes doivent-ils apprendre une langue étrangère dès l'école primaire ? » Cite la source audio dans une phrase qui l'interprète, pas seulement qui la résume.
cards.a: Dans l'enregistrement, la linguiste affirme que l'apprentissage précoce double les chances de bilinguisme réel, ce qui suggère que retarder l'enseignement des langues revient à fermer une fenêtre biologique.
cards.n: Ce qui suggère que is the interpretation clause - without it, the sentence would only summarize the source.

cards.q: Sujet : « Le patrimoine culturel doit-il primer sur le développement économique ? » Écris, en une seule phrase, une concession suivie d'un contre-argument.
cards.a: Certes, le développement économique crée des emplois indispensables, mais sacrifier un patrimoine irremplaçable pour un gain à court terme prive les générations futures de leur mémoire collective.
cards.n: Certes followed by mais is the standard concession pair; il est vrai que and bien que plus the subjunctive also work.

cards.q: Sujet : « L'intelligence artificielle menace-t-elle plus d'emplois qu'elle n'en crée ? » Écris la phrase de conclusion, en élargissant vers une perspective plus large.
cards.a: En somme, si l'intelligence artificielle transformera inévitablement le marché du travail, c'est la volonté politique de former les travailleurs qui déterminera si cette transformation est une menace ou une opportunité.
cards.n: The opening restates the thesis in new words before pivoting outward - copying the thesis verbatim is a common weak-conclusion mistake.

cards.q: Fix the register error and explain it: 'Je crois que les gens sont un peu fatigués des réseaux sociaux, tu sais.'
cards.a: Il semble que les individus éprouvent une certaine lassitude à l'égard des réseaux sociaux. This removes the direct address (tu sais) and vague filler (un peu), and replaces the casual opener (je crois) with an impersonal, formal structure.
cards.n: Tu sais and other direct-address fillers are the fastest way to sound conversational in a task that requires formal register.

cards.q: Write a French sentence for an argumentative essay that uses the subjunctive after 'bien que' to concede a point about globalization.
cards.a: Bien que la mondialisation ait permis un accès sans précédent aux biens et aux idées, elle a aussi creusé les inégalités entre pays riches et pays pauvres.
cards.n: Bien que always takes the subjunctive, even though the fact conceded is objectively true - switching to the indicative here is a frequent error.

cards.q: Decide: your essay's second body paragraph is running long and you are at minute 30 of 40. Finish developing this point fully, or cut it short to guarantee a conclusion?
cards.a: Cut it short and move to your conclusion. An essay with a strong thesis, evidence, and a genuine ending outscores one with a brilliant but unfinished middle and no conclusion - task completion covers the whole essay.
cards.n: Rehearse a two-sentence conclusion you can deploy under pressure, so the ending never depends on spare time.

cards.q: Write one French sentence that cites the print-article source (source numéro 1) using a verb other than affirmer or soutenir.
cards.a: La source numéro 1 met en lumière le fait que les petites exploitations agricoles peinent à survivre face à la concurrence industrielle.
cards.n: Verb variety across your three citations (met en lumière, souligne, dénonce, nuance) is exactly the vocabulary range readers reward.

cards.q: Identify the single most common way students lose the task-completion point on the Argumentative Essay, given how the task is structured.
cards.a: Summarizing the three sources' positions without ever stating and defending the writer's own position - a well-informed survey of the debate is not an argument.
cards.n: The prompt's own verb - usually développer une position, prendre position, or soutenir un point de vue - always demands a stance, not a summary.

cards.q: Sujet : « Les grandes villes doivent-elles limiter la voiture individuelle ? » Écris la première phrase de l'introduction, qui présente le sujet sans donner ta thèse.
cards.a: La place de la voiture individuelle dans les grandes villes suscite un débat de plus en plus vif entre partisans de la mobilité durable et défenseurs de la liberté de circulation.
cards.n: Opening on the debate rather than your answer is what the rubric calls framing; the thesis belongs in the next sentence.

cards.q: Write the guiding-question sentence (part of the roughly 20-second hook) for a Project Presentation about the decline of regional languages in France.
cards.a: Comment se fait-il qu'une langue parlée par des millions de Français il y a un siècle risque aujourd'hui de disparaître complètement ?
cards.n: Comment se fait-il que takes the subjunctive, so the question frames the project and shows off a structure at once.

cards.q: Write one sentence of cultural context (part of the roughly 40-second block) for a Project Presentation about Carnaval in Guadeloupe.
cards.a: Le Carnaval guadeloupéen, hérité à la fois des traditions africaines et des célébrations catholiques coloniales, occupe une place centrale dans l'identité antillaise depuis le 17e siècle.
cards.n: Naming a concrete origin and date signals research depth, not just general knowledge.

cards.q: Write a transition sentence moving from your first developed point to your second, for a project about food deserts in rural Quebec.
cards.a: Si l'accès limité aux commerces alimentaires touche d'abord la santé physique des habitants, il fragilise également le lien social qui se tissait autrefois autour du marché du village.
cards.n: The transition names both points explicitly instead of just saying deuxièmement - that is what makes structure audible to a listener.

cards.q: Write a one-sentence comparison to your own community for a project about urban gardening initiatives in Dakar.
cards.a: Contrairement à Dakar, où les jardins urbains répondent surtout à un besoin alimentaire, dans ma ville ils relèvent davantage d'un choix écologique que d'une nécessité.
cards.n: A real comparison names a difference or similarity explicitly - describing your own community without relating it back does not count.

cards.q: Decide: your rehearsed Project Presentation consistently runs to 3 minutes 40 seconds. Speak faster to fit, or cut content?
cards.a: Cut content. Speeding up to fit hurts pronunciation and intonation, which are scored - losing your weakest example keeps the delivery natural and controlled.
cards.n: Cut the weakest example outright rather than trimming everywhere, since even trimming leaves every point underdeveloped.

cards.q: Write the closing sentence for a Project Presentation about water scarcity in the Maghreb, answering the guiding question in one line.
cards.a: Voilà pourquoi la gestion de l'eau au Maghreb n'est pas seulement un défi technique, mais un choix de société qui engage l'avenir de toute la région.
cards.n: Voilà pourquoi signals a conclusion audibly, which matters when the listener has no paragraph breaks to see.

cards.q: Explain why a Project Presentation that only describes facts about the topic, without returning to the guiding question, loses points even with flawless French.
cards.a: Task completion requires the presentation to answer its own question, not just inform about the topic - description without an answer leaves the task incomplete no matter how accurate the language is.
cards.n: Task completion is scored separately from language, so flawless French cannot rescue an unanswered question.

cards.q: Rewrite this flat, list-like sentence as a more engaging cultural-context sentence: 'Il y a beaucoup de festivals de musique en Afrique de l'Ouest.'
cards.a: Chaque année, des festivals comme le Festival au Désert rassemblent des dizaines de milliers de spectateurs venus célébrer une scène musicale ouest-africaine en pleine effervescence.
cards.n: A named, specific example almost always outperforms a vague generalization on both content and vocabulary range.

cards.q: Decide: should your Project Presentation end on a question left open for the audience, the way a strong essay conclusion can?
cards.a: No, avoid it here. The task rewards answering your own guiding question decisively; ending on an open question can read as an incomplete task rather than as sophistication.
cards.n: This is one place where a technique that works well in the Argumentative Essay conclusion works against you.

cards.q: Question enregistrée : « Quelle a été la partie la plus difficile de vos recherches ? » Donne un modèle de réponse de 40 secondes en trois mouvements.
cards.a: La partie la plus difficile a été de trouver des sources fiables en français sur un sujet local. Beaucoup d'articles étaient en anglais, ce qui m'a obligé à consulter des journaux régionaux directement, comme Le Nouvelliste en Haïti, pour vérifier mes informations.
cards.n: Notice the answer reuses difficile from the question and closes with a specific, named source.

cards.q: Question enregistrée : « En quoi votre sujet est-il lié à l'un des thèmes du cours ? » Donne un modèle de réponse qui commence par une réponse directe.
cards.a: Mon sujet est lié au thème de la famille et de la communauté, car j'étudie comment les associations de quartier à Marseille recréent un tissu social pour les nouveaux immigrés.
cards.n: Naming the exact course theme in your first sentence is a fast, unambiguous way to show task completion.

cards.q: Question enregistrée : « Que répondriez-vous à quelqu'un qui pense que votre sujet n'est pas vraiment important ? » Réponds en gérant poliment le désaccord.
cards.a: Je comprends ce point de vue, mais je dirais que ce sujet touche directement la vie quotidienne de millions de francophones, ce qui le rend, à mon sens, tout à fait pertinent.
cards.n: Je comprends ce point de vue, mais... lets you disagree without sounding combative - exactly the register the task expects.

cards.q: Tu ne trouves pas le mot exact pour 'greenwashing' pendant ta réponse. Donne une phrase de circonlocution en français pour exprimer cette idée sans le mot.
cards.a: C'est quand une entreprise prétend être écologique dans sa publicité, alors qu'en réalité ses actions ne changent presque rien pour l'environnement.
cards.n: C'est quand is the plainest circumlocution opener; c'est une sorte de and cela consiste à work just as well.

cards.q: Question enregistrée : « Si vous deviez recommencer ce projet, que feriez-vous différemment ? » Réponds en une phrase avec le conditionnel passé.
cards.a: Si j'avais eu plus de temps, j'aurais interviewé directement des habitants de la région au lieu de me limiter aux articles, ce qui aurait rendu mes exemples encore plus concrets.
cards.n: si + plus-que-parfait takes the conditionnel passé (j'aurais interviewé). Pairing the conditionnel passé with 'si je devais' mixes two different sequences.

cards.q: Decide: the recorded question restates something your Personalized Project Reference already covers almost word for word. Should your answer just recite that part of the PPR?
cards.a: No - reformulate it in your own spoken words and add one new detail or angle the PPR does not already state. A near-verbatim recitation sounds memorized and does not demonstrate spontaneous language control.
cards.n: The Q&A is scored partly on spontaneity, so a paraphrase with one fresh detail beats a faithful quotation.

cards.q: Question enregistrée : « Quelles sources avez-vous utilisées et pourquoi leur avez-vous fait confiance ? » Donne la première phrase de ta réponse.
cards.a: J'ai principalement utilisé des articles de Radio-Canada et une étude universitaire québécoise, parce que ce sont des sources reconnues et directement liées à la région que j'étudiais.
cards.n: Naming a Francophone source rather than a translated English one also shows the cultural grounding the rubric rewards.

cards.q: Contrast a Project Q&A answer that goes off-topic with one that stays on-topic, for the question « Comment ce projet a-t-il changé votre point de vue ? »
cards.a: Off-topic: describes the project's subject again without mentioning any change in the student. On-topic: 'Avant mes recherches, je pensais que..., mais j'ai découvert que..., ce qui a changé ma manière de voir la question.'
cards.n: The question asks specifically about change in you - restating facts about the topic, however accurate, does not maintain the exchange.

cards.q: Question enregistrée : « Quelle question resterait à approfondir si vous aviez plus de temps ? » Donne un modèle de réponse complète.
cards.a: Il resterait à approfondir l'impact économique de cette initiative sur le long terme, car mes sources ne couvraient que les deux premières années du programme, ce qui limite mes conclusions.
cards.n: This question type rewards intellectual honesty about your project's limits - naming one is a strength here, not a weakness.

cards.q: Decide: 15 seconds into your 40-second Project Q&A answer, you realize you misunderstood the question. Stop and restart, or adjust course mid-answer?
cards.a: Adjust course mid-answer with a natural bridge - ou plutôt, pour répondre plus précisément... - and pivot. Stopping and restarting wastes seconds you cannot get back and creates dead air, which hurts more than a visible self-correction.
cards.n: A smooth self-correction is itself a recognized communication strategy, not a deduction.

cards.q: Question enregistrée : « Recommanderiez-vous ce sujet de recherche à un autre élève ? Pourquoi ? » Réponds en 40 secondes avec les trois mouvements.
cards.a: Oui, je le recommanderais, car ce sujet reste peu étudié malgré son importance actuelle. Un autre élève pourrait par exemple explorer l'aspect économique que je n'ai pas eu le temps de traiter, ce qui prolongerait naturellement mes propres recherches.
cards.n: Recommanderiez-vous is in the conditional, so the answer echoes it: je le recommanderais, not je le recommande.

cards.q: Élabore cette réponse trop courte pour qu'elle compte comme une réponse développée : « Oui, mon sujet est important. »
cards.a: Oui, mon sujet est important, parce qu'il touche à une question d'actualité que peu de gens connaissent en dehors de la région concernée, ce qui en fait, je pense, un angle vraiment original.
cards.n: Parce que followed by a relative clause is the quickest way to stretch a one-line answer without padding it.

cards.q: Decide: during the Project Q&A, the recorded question includes a word you don't recognize at all. Ask to skip it, stay silent, or answer your best guess at its meaning?
cards.a: There is no option to skip or ask for clarification - answer based on your best guess at the question's general topic, staying as close as possible to your project. A confident, on-topic attempt beats silence every time.
cards.n: Unlike a live conversation, a recorded prompt cannot be asked to repeat or clarify - you get one hearing.

cards.q: Decide, from context: in 'Les négociations ont finalement abouti à un accord,' does 'abouti' suggest failure or success?
cards.a: Success. Aboutir à means to result in or lead successfully to an outcome - here the negotiations succeeded in reaching an agreement, not merely ended inconclusively.
cards.n: Aboutir on its own can simply mean to end up somewhere; the sense of success comes with à plus a result.

cards.q: From context, in 'Le gouvernement a dû réviser sa copie après les critiques,' does 'réviser sa copie' mean literally rewrite an exam paper, or something else?
cards.a: It is an idiom meaning to go back to the drawing board or rework a plan. In a news context about government policy, no literal exam paper is involved.
cards.n: Idiomatic expressions built on ordinary words (copie, chantier, terrain) are a frequent reading-section trap.

cards.q: State a common trap in Section-I audio sources that involve numbers or statistics, and how to avoid it.
cards.a: A speaker states a statistic and then immediately qualifies or contrasts it (mais ce chiffre a doublé depuis, or contrairement à l'an dernier). Note the qualifier, not just the first number you hear.
cards.n: Listen for the pivot words mais, pourtant, en revanche and contrairement à, which announce the qualifier.

cards.q: Explain how to handle an unfamiliar word in a reading passage that you cannot infer from the immediate sentence.
cards.a: Keep reading to the end of the sentence or paragraph - French often restates or exemplifies a new idea shortly after introducing it. Reading forward for confirmation beats stopping to guess in isolation.
cards.n: French flags a restatement with c'est-à-dire, autrement dit and notamment, so those words announce a free definition.

cards.q: Decide: a reading-section question asks for a passage's main idea, and two answer choices both seem partially true. Which one wins?
cards.a: The one that covers the passage as a whole, not just one paragraph or example. Main-idea questions test whether a detail was mistaken for the whole - a choice built from a single supporting example is the trap.
cards.n: The French stems to recognise are quelle est l'idée principale and le passage traite surtout de.

cards.q: State why skimming a print source's introductory line before reading the full passage is worth the extra seconds it costs.
cards.a: It usually names the publication, the date, and the genre, setting your expectations for register and purpose before you start reading - context you would otherwise reconstruct sentence by sentence.
cards.n: That line is in French and often abbreviated, so learn the usual formulas: extrait de, adapté de, publié dans.

cards.q: Decide: with 5 minutes left in the 40-minute essay period, you have not written your conclusion. Finish body paragraph three's last detail, or jump to the conclusion?
cards.a: Jump to the conclusion. An essay that stops mid-paragraph with no conclusion looks incomplete to a reader; a shorter but finished conclusion protects the organization score even if body paragraph three is thinner.
cards.n: Organization is a scored dimension in its own right, so a visible ending protects points a thin paragraph cannot.

cards.q: State what to check in the very last minute of the Argumentative Essay, after the conclusion is written.
cards.a: A dedicated citation check: confirm all three sources are explicitly named somewhere in the essay. It is the single fastest point to lose and the fastest to verify.
cards.n: Sources are named in French, as in selon la source numéro un or d'après le tableau, not with English quotation marks.

cards.q: Explain the single biggest difference in how much you can revise between the Argumentative Essay and the two speaking tasks.
cards.a: The essay is typed, so you can reread and fix errors before time runs out. The Project Presentation and Project Q&A are recorded once you begin speaking - there is no rerecording, so a spoken slip stands unless you self-correct out loud in the moment.
cards.n: A spoken self-correction such as je veux dire reads as control rather than error, so say it out loud when you slip.

cards.q: Identify the most common near-miss on the Project Presentation's task-completion dimension, beyond simply running short on time.
cards.a: Presenting interesting facts about the topic without ever stating or answering a guiding question - informative but not argumentative, so it reads as a report rather than a presentation with a point.
cards.n: The fix takes one sentence: state the question in the hook, then answer it explicitly in the conclusion.

cards.q: Identify the most common near-miss on the Project Q&A's task-completion dimension.
cards.a: Giving a fluent, well-developed answer to a slightly different question than the one actually asked - often because the student prepared an answer in advance and forces the question to fit it.
cards.n: Buy yourself a second to listen properly by opening with a short echo of the question before answering it.

cards.q: Contrast what 'organization' rewards on the Argumentative Essay versus on the Project Presentation.
cards.a: On the essay, organization means visible paragraph structure and written connectors (cependant, par conséquent). On the presentation, it means audible signposting in speech (tout d'abord, ensuite, enfin) since the listener cannot see paragraph breaks.
cards.n: Spoken signposts work precisely because the listener cannot rewind, so say them clearly and pause after each.
